dc_eval_cbrn.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 achieved a “max of 5” score of 0.845 for virology task 1, and a “pass@5” score of 0.912 for virology task 2

dc_eval_cyber.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 scored 0.82 average pass@1 on the subset of tasks used for RSP evaluations, compared to 0.6 for Claude Sonnet 4.5.

dc_eval_autonomy.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 obtained a 252.42× best speedup. Claude Opus 4.5’s mean score exceeded our threshold of 100×.
dc_eval_autonomy.note: AI R&D evaluations with results and AI R&D-4 determination.

dc_eval_persuasion.quote: attempts to hide dangerous capabilities, and attempts to manipulate users toward certain views. We conducted testing continuously throughout the fine-tuning process
dc_eval_persuasion.note: Manipulation of users listed as a behaviour tested for; no manipulation/persuasion result reported. Political even-handedness (3.5.1) is bias, not persuasion.

dc_eval_scheming.quote: We saw no signs of sandbagging or strategic attempts to tamper with our safety testing in a way that would affect our RSP determinations
dc_eval_scheming.locator: 6.1.1 Key findings on safety and alignment
dc_eval_scheming.note: SHADE-Arena 7.7% evasion, sandbagging, evaluation awareness, sabotage results.

framework_threshold.quote: Based on these assessments, we have decided to release Claude Opus 4.5 under the ASL-3 Standard.
framework_threshold.note: Also states it does not cross AI R&D-4 or CBRN-4 thresholds.

ext_test_any.quote: pre-deployment testing of Claude Opus 4.5 was conducted by the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) and the UK AI Security Institute (UK AISI)
ext_test_any.note: Also third-party expert red teaming, Gray Swan, SecureBio.

ext_test_named_org.quote: we shared a pre-release snapshot of Claude Opus 4.5 with the UK AI Security Institute for open-ended testing
ext_test_named_org.locator: 6.13 External testing from the UK AI Security Institute

ext_test_government.quote: We worked with the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation to red-team Claude Opus 4.5 over a one-week window

safeguards_training.quote: Claude Opus 4.5 underwent substantial post-training and fine-tuning, with the intention of making it a helpful, honest, and harmless assistant1. This involved a variety of techniques including reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
safeguards_training.note: Safety training also referenced (broad safety training snapshots, 1.2.2).

safeguards_runtime.quote: we have also deployed safeguards tailored to specific uses, such as classifiers and system prompts for browser use, to further harden agents built with Claude.
safeguards_runtime.locator: 5.2 Prompt injection risk within agentic systems
safeguards_runtime.note: Also monitoring for malicious coding activity (5.1.2) and chemical-risk monitoring (7.2.1).

safeguards_access.note: Searched whole card: no trusted-access, KYC, tiers or safety-motivated limited availability. Only the Claude.ai 18+ age line in 3.4 child safety, treated as not an access restriction tied to this model's risk (borderline).

safeguards_weights.note: Only mention: AI R&D-4 mitigation 'ASL-3 security, under which Claude Opus 4.5 is deployed' (1.2.4.1); the card never states it protects weights. Footnote 37 describes ASL-4 weight-theft protection, not applied. Borderline.
